# Yantra (यन्त्र)

> A personal developer control plane: one interface over the workspaces, AI coding agents and
> machines on a Tailscale mesh. Ask for a workspace and it picks a machine, opens the tmux session,
> and resumes the agent. Rust daemon, CLI and per-machine agent; TypeScript web UI. Personal-scale
> and deliberately so — its niche is pre-existing, personally-owned, heterogeneous machines that must
> never be destroyed, which is the case Coder and DevPod cannot represent.

**Read `tracker.md` first.** It is the single source of truth for project state, and it wins over
anything else — including this file — when they disagree.

Each crate carries its own `CLAUDE.md`, `tracker.md`, `llms.txt` and `README.md`. Start at the crate
you are changing rather than reading the root documents end to end. **The invariants live in the
crate trackers** — non-obvious rules, most earned by a bug that presented as something else, and
[`tracker.md` §1b](tracker.md) indexes which crate holds which. They are the highest-value thing in
the repo.

## Start here

- [tracker.md](tracker.md): project state — milestones, open tasks, decisions, open questions, risks, and an index of where the invariants live.
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): how to work in this repo — think before coding, surgical changes, and what "verification" means here (a real sshd and a real tmux, never a mock).
- [README.md](README.md): what Yantra is, for a human — install, usage, the workspace schema.
- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md): the structure, the `up` sequence, the trust boundaries and where the live risks sit, as rendered diagrams. The fastest way to orient.

## Crates

- [yantra-core](crates/yantra-core/llms.txt): all the orchestration — ssh, tmux, agents, inventory, workspaces. Never prints, never exits. This is where nearly all the code is.
- [yantra](crates/yantra/llms.txt): the CLI. Renders and chooses exit codes; decides nothing.
- [yantrad](crates/yantrad/llms.txt): the daemon. An axum server binding only this machine's Tailscale addresses: a read-only JSON API over a background snapshot, the writes (`POST /heartbeat`, `new`/`edit`/`up`/`down`/`resume`/`delete` per workspace, a re-check that asks one machine now, a spend figure summed on the far side, the ntfy relay written to the file its unit reads ([ADR-0021](docs/adr/0021-the-relay-is-written-to-an-environment-file.md)), and a beacon saying a dashboard is open — all authorised by Tailscale identity), a WebSocket that bridges a workspace's session to a browser under the same authorisation, and the dashboard itself.
- [yantra-agent](crates/yantra-agent/llms.txt): the per-machine heartbeat — seven probes, a 10 s loop and a hand-written POST. It has a unit on Linux and a recipe that installs it.

## Decisions

Accepted ADRs are immutable. If one is wrong, propose a superseding ADR — do not quietly build
something else.

- [docs/adr/](docs/adr/): the ones that constrain most code are [0005](docs/adr/0005-core-logic-in-a-library-crate.md) (library crate), [0006](docs/adr/0006-ssh-exec-transport.md) (ssh transport), [0009](docs/adr/0009-machine-names-are-ssh-destinations.md) (machine names) and [0011](docs/adr/0011-claude-code-runs-as-a-tui-in-tmux.md) (the agent is a TUI).
- [docs/research/](docs/research/): dated research notes, one per topic — its [README](docs/research/README.md) indexes them. Evidence as of their access date, not eternal truth — re-verify anything version-sensitive.
- [docs/research/13-dashboard-revamp-and-github.md](docs/research/13-dashboard-revamp-and-github.md): read this before proposing anything about the dashboard, a router, or a Git provider. It measures what the page is against the founding UI principle, prices a GitHub clone against the decisions it collides with — persistence, secrets, and Tailscale identity — and records that of the two machines online, the one holding a working GitHub credential has no sshd and the one reachable over ssh has no credential, so nothing on this fleet can be cloned to today.
- [docs/design/](docs/design/): proposed designs, each ending in work units sized to be picked up one at a time. [00-plan.md](docs/design/00-plan.md) is the index and the order — what each document below settles, what is left, and why the visual pass is written last and from rendered options rather than from a brief. [01-dashboard.md](docs/design/01-dashboard.md) is the GUI-first control plane — routes, the reconcile-before-launch probe, Claude Code's `/rc`, what the browser terminal must do to count as interactive, and why cloning is provider-agnostic while browsing is not. [02-setup.md](docs/design/02-setup.md) is provisioning — Yantra does what it can and names what it cannot, and `yantra doctor` is the one probe the dashboard, the installer and an agent all read. [03-dashboard-surface.md](docs/design/03-dashboard-surface.md) is the half D1 left open — the fleet page grouped by who must act next, navigation, density, state marks, words, failure, weight and motion, settled in a 27-question interview and written against tokens so pigment can land later as `index.css`. [04-workspace-creation.md](docs/design/04-workspace-creation.md) is creating a workspace by choosing rather than typing, and it is worth reading for one measurement: a whole-home `find` costs **8.5 s** on this fleet's Mac against 0.026 s on its Linux box, so the directory is walked one level at a time at a probe's price rather than swept. [05-workspace-page.md](docs/design/05-workspace-page.md) is the workspace page — three tabs carried in `?view=`, the transcript read on request and windowed, spend without a picker, and every tab naming the machine it could not reach; its measurement is that a tool call's **input already crosses the ssh wire and the parse throws it away**, so *edited web/src/api.ts* costs nothing the daemon is not already paying, while forwarding every input whole would add 2.5× the projection. [06-sessions-attention-spend.md](docs/design/06-sessions-attention-spend.md) is what the fleet owes a reader outside one workspace — the GitHub queue as a band inside *Needs you* with its own 300 s clock, an unclaimed session that can be attached to and killed but never adopted, no fleet spend total, and the reasoning for the ADR that lets a socket address a session rather than a workspace; its finding is that **three of those readings are already served by the daemon and no file in the browser asks for them**. Proposals: they open no rows.

## Optional

- [docs/development.md](docs/development.md): local setup and daily commands.
- [docs/appliance.md](docs/appliance.md): installing and updating the always-on box — what it needs first, and why the replacement is a rename. [install.sh](install.sh) is the fetch-and-verify half of it: a published release onto a fresh box, enabling nothing and enrolling nothing, run twice against a real systemd by [crates/yantrad/tests/installer.rs](crates/yantrad/tests/installer.rs). [provision.sh](provision.sh) is the other half: it reads `yantra doctor --json`, enables each unit whose precondition holds, and turns everything left into a numbered step with its command. One of those steps is `yantra ssh-identity`, which prepares the box's own key and `~/.ssh/config` and prints the public key to place — a verb the owner invokes, because whether generating it is Yantra's job at all is still unconfirmed ([docs/design/02-setup.md](docs/design/02-setup.md) §2).
- [docs/machines.md](docs/machines.md): the actual fleet this is developed against.
- [docs/vision.md](docs/vision.md): the long-range shape, including the hardware panel.
- [docs/session-log.md](docs/session-log.md): one line per working session, append-only. Newest last.
- [docs/archive/m0-m1.md](docs/archive/m0-m1.md): closed milestones M0 and M1. History, not current state.
- [docs/archive/m2-m3.md](docs/archive/m2-m3.md): closed milestones M2 and M3, with the evidence behind each task.
- [docs/archive/m4-m5.md](docs/archive/m4-m5.md): closed milestones M4 and M5 — the dashboard, the heartbeat agent and control from the phone — plus the rolling status narrative `tracker.md §0` carried until 2026-08-03.
- [docs/archive/m6-m7.md](docs/archive/m6-m7.md): the closed rows of M6 (terminal in browser) and M7 (appliance), plus the preamble `tracker.md §3` opened them under. Both milestones are still open; nothing below waits on a row here.
- [docs/archive/m11-m13.md](docs/archive/m11-m13.md): closed milestones M11 (work inbox), M12 (sessions and cost) and M13 (the dashboard you can work in), all closed 2026-09-04. M13 closed as buildable work done; its phone clause is unmeasured.
